newsitem.title: JAPAN: SWIMMING - POLL, DOLAN CHARGE INTO PAN PACIFIC FIN.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING - POLL, DOLAN CHARGE INTO PAN PACIFIC FIN.

text.p: Olympic champions Claudia Poll of Costa Rica, Tom Dolan of the United States and Australian Susan O'Neill led qualifiers on the first day of the Pan Pacific Championships on Sunday.
Poll topped the morning heats in the women's 200 metres freestyle with a time of two minutes 1.01 seconds, which was outside of the 1:58.16 she swam to win the event in Atlanta.
Dolan, who won the gold in the 400 individual medley at the Summer Olympics, swam a lifetime best of 1:49.83 to top all qualifiers in the men's 200 freestyle.
Australian Michael Klim, who turns 20 on Wednesday, was second (1:49.91) just ahead of American Josh Davis (1:49.92).

One of the most anticipated clashes in the finals on Sunday night will be between O'Neill and Misty Hyman of the United States in the women's 200 butterfly. O'Neill, who won the event in Atlanta, topped her heat with a time of 2:09.96, while Hyman won her heat with a time of 2:10.61.
Hyman used her unique start and underwater fish kick to swim almost 30 metres of the first lap underwater, emerging nearly five metres ahead of her competitors.

Mai Nakamura gave the Japanese fans someone to cheer, edging home first in the women's 100 backstroke heats with a time of 1:01.72, ahead of Americans Catherine Fox (1:02.03) and Lea Loveless (1:02.06).

Russian-born Lenny Krayzelburg was the top qualifier in the men's 100 backstroke for the United States. Krayzelburg, who was born in Odessa and became a U.S. citizen in 1995, had a time of 54.97 to beat compatriot Neil Walker (55.42) and Mark Versfeld of Canada (55.69).
American Ugur Taner was the fastest in the men's 200 butterfly heats with a time of 1:57.94. Thomas Malchow of the U.S. was second (1.58:29) and Australian Scott Goodman third (1:58.62).
About 300 swimmers from 23 countries and regions are competing in the Pan Pacific meet, one of the last important meets on the swimming calendar prior to next January's world championships.
